findings.title: Autocast menu and badge never appear when ability gizmos are drawn shrunk (pawns with many abilities)
findings.detail: Command_Ability sets shrinkable=true. When the gizmo grid needs more than one row and there are 2+ shrinkable commands, GizmoGridDrawer draws them through Command.GizmoOnGUIShrunk, which calls GizmoOnGUIInt directly and never reaches Command_Ability.GizmoOnGUI. So neither Patch_CommandAbility_Autocast.Prefix nor Postfix runs: no right-click menu, no badge, and vanilla's 'disabled' message still shows on cooldown, which is the case this file says it fixes. Add a prefix/postfix on Command.GizmoOnGUIShrunk (where it is declared), filtered to __instance is Command_Ability, with a size x size rect at topLeft, reusing Offers/OpenMenu and the badge code. The corpus is silent: no scanned mod patches either method.

findings.title: Undrafted autocast throws away the interrupted work job instead of resuming it
findings.detail: Vanilla starts a constant-tree job with InterruptForced and resumeCurJobAfterwards:false, so a colonist interrupted mid-job (sowing, cleaning, hauling with empty hands) loses that job and picks work again from scratch after the cast. Usually it picks the same work, so nothing breaks, but reservations are dropped and progress on toil-based jobs restarts. If that matters, enqueue a copy of the interrupted job with a fresh loadID, the way the drafted AttackStatic path already does (AbilityAI.cs:774-781).

findings.title: A drafted pawn is 'in combat' if any hostile pawn is anywhere on the map, fogged ones included
findings.detail: InCombat counts `drafted && Enemies.Count > 0`, and the attack-target cache does not skip hostiles in unexplored, fogged areas (for example the inside of an unopened ancient complex). A drafted pawn could therefore run InCombat-only workers and skip OutOfCombat ones while no enemy can actually be seen. This is my opinion and I have not confirmed it in play. A Fogged() check in IsEnemy, applied only on the drafted path, would close it.

findings.title: Saving skips only Discarded pawns, so a pawn that exists but isn't saved elsewhere leaves an unresolved-reference warning on load
findings.detail: ExposeData saves every non-Discarded pawn key. A pawn that is destroyed but neither discarded nor in WorldPawns is not saved anywhere else, so the Scribe_References entry fails to resolve on load and LoadedObjectDirectory logs a Warning (not an error). The PostLoadInit null check then drops the entry, so it heals after one load. Also skipping pawns that are Destroyed and not in Find.WorldPawns at save time would avoid the warning.

findings.title: File header still says workers only run for non-colonists
findings.detail: Line 12's cost note says a worker 'only runs for a pawn that is not a colonist'. Since this change, the player's drafted pawns and (with UndraftedAutocast) undrafted pawns also reach TryFindTarget through CanActNowPlayer. Change that sentence to say player pawns are evaluated too, and that undrafted ones only try workers where WorksUndrafted is true. The cost reasoning in the header no longer covers the colony.

findings.title: InMelee(ctx) summary describes a different check
findings.detail: The summary says 'the nearest enemy within 1.5 tiles that is fighting the pawn in melee', but the overload just calls InMelee(ctx, pawn). That checks mindState.meleeThreat: hurt in melee within RecentTicks by someone still within 1.5 tiles. Copy the second overload's summary onto it.
